post.description:
Before showing the "choose your password" form: whose link is it, and does
it still work?
Use an invite or reset link: set the password, end other sessions, sign in.

The project page's tour, finished or closed: not offered again to this account
on any device ("Ver tour" in the staff bar replays it).

Emails a link to choose a new password to this office's account with that
address. The same answer whether or not there is one, and no sooner: every
request takes RESET_ANSWER_AT, and the email goes after the response, so
neither the answer nor its timing tells who has an account.

get.description:
How full the office's Google account is, as the old site showed: asked
of Google on each visit to the Drive settings, never stored.

put.description: The logo; with an SVG, also `png`, the painel's drawing of it (for email).
The logo for dark mode (pages show it only with the usual one).

delete.description: Dark mode shows the usual logo again.

put.description:
The PNG of an SVG logo uploaded before PNGs were drawn (the painel sends it
when it sees `logo_needs_png`).

delete.description:
Only a pending invite: its account and links go (removing staff who are in
comes later, A36).

post.description:
Emails an invite link to the address given, as a new member. The same answer
whatever the address, and no sooner than JOIN_ANSWER_AT: someone with an account
already gets nothing (they can sign in, or use "Esqueceu a senha?").

A draft goes live: its page opens to anyone with the link. New projects are
published at once (A35), so only a draft left over shows the staff bar's
button: one created by the previous release during a deploy, or an open tab
of it (A30). Publishing twice changes nothing.

schema.title: Response Detail Types Api Detail Types Get

put.description:
The page shows one meeting, the next: this sets it (a new one, or the
upcoming one changed).
A stage's note to the client ("Recado"); empty removes it.

post.description:
At the end: a built-in stage (not already in the project) or the office's own.
A new stage is open, so a completed project is active again (stages complete
independently).

patch.description: A built-in stage renamed becomes the office's own, keeping its description.

delete.description:
The stage leaves the page; its folder and files stay in Drive. The stages
after it move up, and their folders are renumbered.

post.description: Swap with its neighbour. The current stage stays the same stage.

put.description:
Every stage in its new place at once (edit mode's "Reordenar etapas"), their
folders renumbered. The current stage stays the same stage, wherever it goes.

Mark a stage as completed, or reopen it, whatever the other stages are. The
client sees it at once; "Atualizado" moves. A completed stage is recorded for
the client's email (A32). The last stage completed completes the project (an
active one), and reopening one makes a completed project active again.

"Concluir projeto": an active project whose stages are all completed. Staff
are asked when they complete the last stage, and can do it later; the client
sees it at once and is told by email (A32).

post.description:
The previous release's progress, for a tab still running its code during a
deploy (A30); remove in the release after independent stages. "advance" and
"complete" complete the first open stage; "back" and "reopen" reopen the last
completed one.

Which of these names match a document in the stage's folder, so the page
can ask "É uma nova versão de Planta.pdf?" (A25).

The bytes go from the browser to Google, past the app; when sending fails
for good, the browser reports it here, so it is logged with the office and the
operation, and staff get the support code that the log line carries.
The file stays in Drive, renamed "_name", which the page doesn't show.

Into another stage's folder, at its top. The file keeps its identity, so
it is not "new" again and sends no email (A10).
The client types the project's password once per device (A06).

Languages the site's own text is translated into. Text an office writes
itself is shown as written.

ReaderStatus.title: ReaderStatus
ReaderStatus.description: The reader identity's access to the office's folder (pages, downloads).

StaffView.title: StaffView
StaffView.description: Only for the office's signed-in staff: what the staff bar needs.

UpdateOut.title: UpdateOut
UpdateOut.description:
One entry of the page's "Atualizações" (A28), newest first. The page words
it from what it shows now (the stage's title and note, the meeting).

WriterStatus.title: WriterStatus
WriterStatus.description: The office's own grant, used to create folders and upload.
